newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian troops scour frontier for U.S. oilman.
newsitem.headline: Colombian troops scour frontier for U.S. oilman.

text.p: Colombian troops scoured a remote region of the eastern border with Venezuela on Wednesday in search of a kidnapped U.S. oilman, military sources said.

Gerald Schaffer of Houston-based Oil Productions Co. was snatched on Friday while on a fishing trip in Venezuela's southwest Apure state and is thought to have been brought into Colombia by suspected leftist rebels.
Colombia's top anti-kidnap official Alberto Villamizar pledged all necessary measures to secure Schaffer's release.

"I am in constant touch with the U.S. Embassy in Bogota and with the Venezuelan authorities. It would not be the first time that guerrillas have kidnapped somebody in Venezuela and brought them back to Colombia," Villamizar said.
"We're carrying out checks but the eastern plains region (along the border) is vast. This case worries us and we will take all necessary steps to solve the case," he added.
Schaffer's companion, a Venzuelan, was also taken along with the Cessna 310 light aircraft in which both had been travelling.

Villamizar said rebels may have kidnapped Schaffer with the aim of stealing his plane, citing the case of a group of Venezuelans travelling in two light aircraft who were seized two months ago and later released unharmed.
U.S. geologist Frank Pescatori of New Jersey, kidnapped by gunmen near a coal mining site in Colombia's northern Guajira province in mid-December, has not yet been released.
More than 1,300 people were officially reported kidnapped last year in Colombia, the kidnap capital of the world. Excluding Venezuelans, Villamizar said, about 20 of them were foreigners.
